Acoustic monitoring · terminal cranes

The crane tells you it is failing. Nobody is listening.

A probe in the machinery house listens without a break, learns how this particular machine sounds in every phase of its cycle, and scores every second of audio. When something departs from the norm, maintenance knows within seconds — not at the next inspection.

Start with a single crane → See the field deployment ↓

The risk we take off the table

A crane failure never costs what the part costs.

Nobody measures risk by the price of a component. What matters is when the replacement falls due and what else it takes down on the way. Continuous listening moves the repair out of a breakdown and into a planned window — and that is the whole difference.

Unplanned downtime

A failure does not book an appointment. Caught early, it drops into a maintenance window you already have in the schedule — no vessel reshuffling and no demurrage.

Consequential damage

A worn bearing destroys the shaft and the gearbox. The same fault caught earlier is one component replaced, not a full drive-train overhaul.

The inspection that found nothing

An inspection shows the machine on the day of the inspection. The fault develops over the other 89 days of the quarter — and nobody is listening then.

Arguing with service without evidence

In a dispute with a service provider or the OEM, what counts is the record: the recording, the date, and the trend. That is an argument no operator's impression can overturn.

What we deliver

One device, powerful AI on board.

Sound from every drive assembly reaches a single probe standing in the machinery house. We do not wire up each bearing — the model attributes a deviation to a mechanism, based on that assembly's spectral signature and the cycle phase the deviation occurred in.

AI acoustic probe

A passive, magnet-mounted device that touches neither the structure nor the crane's controls.

  • A very wide band of acoustic signals — audible sound and ultrasound
  • Neural networks running on a dedicated AI accelerator inside the probe
  • Continuous listening, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
  • Recordings stored from day one — available to play back at any time
  • Wired or cellular connectivity — no demands on the terminal's network
  • Installed without drilling, without stopping the machine, without changes to statutory documentation

Powerful AI — on the device, not in the cloud

A dedicated AI accelerator runs inside the probe. One neural network recognises the types of sound a machine makes; a second layer learns the norm for this specific crane and each phase of its cycle. Confirmed and rejected alerts feed back into the model, which is retrained periodically — the system gets better the longer it runs on your site.

Continuous listening instead of a sample

A vibration measurement is a snapshot of the machine at one moment, once a quarter. The probe listens without a break and sees a change on the day it appears — including events that last a second and will not repeat while the inspector is there.

Prediction in real time

The model scores sound as it happens, on site. From raw audio to a finished, attributed alert takes seconds — not a day waiting for cloud processing and not a week for a laboratory report.

One number that says how far this is from normal

For every second of audio the model computes how far that sound sits from the norm learned for this machine and this cycle phase. The same number, collected over weeks, shows whether something is building or whether it was a one-off. Every event keeps its recording, and machines can be compared against each other.

Field deployment

Tauron Ekoenergia: two faults caught by sound alone.

Before we entered a crane machinery house, the same system was running inside a wind turbine nacelle — an enclosed technical space with a gearbox, bearings, a brake and cooling fans. The deployment report was approved by the farm operator.

Deployment

  • 5 Senvion MM92 turbineson a farm of 15 turbines, 30.75 MW
  • A fleet 15 years into servicethe profile where early warning delivers the most
  • Continuous listening, 24 hours a dayAI inference on the device, on site — not in the cloud
  • Validated with the operator's teamscarried out jointly with operations and service

Results

A developing bearing fault

Detected acoustically and confirmed by the operator's service team. Repaired in a planned window instead of an emergency shutdown.

A cooling-fan defect

Picked up by sound alone — beyond the reach of the temperature and vibration sensors the turbine already carried.

  • From raw audio to a finished alert — automatically, within seconds
  • Acoustic monitoring proven in real maintenance decisions
  • Found what temperature sensors, vibration sensors and visual inspection do not show

One platform, many machines

The same platform, the next machine.

The probe is not tied to a type of equipment. Wherever a rotating assembly works inside an enclosed space — a gearbox, bearings, a brake, fans — the physics and the audio pipeline are the same. There is one difference: a turbine turns at a steady rate while a crane works in cycles, so the model learns the cycle phases — otherwise every container lifted would look like an anomaly.

Proven on turbines

A wind turbine nacelle: gearbox, main bearings, brake, cooling system. Deployed with a farm operator, report approved.

Rolling out on cranes

The machinery house of an STS, RMG or RTG crane: hoist, travel gearboxes, brakes, fans, power cabinets. The same probe and the same base model — and because the installation is not a modification of the equipment, the manufacturer's warranty stays intact.

The next machine does not start from zero

The base model is shared across the fleet — a new machine only adds its own layer of normal. Extending to another unit takes weeks, not a new project.

Getting started

Two ways in, both short.

A pilot on one crane

You pick one machine. We fit the probe without stopping it and without changes to the equipment's documentation, listen for a few weeks, and hand over a report on what we heard. Only then do we talk about the rest of the fleet.

Book a pilot →

A meeting with a live demo

An hour at your site or remotely. We show the working system on data from the deployment: what an alert looks like, how you work with history and recordings, what maintenance sees. We answer the technical questions, with no commitment.

Book a meeting →
